av_event.line_text: Isaac: Nah, that sounds actually sick. I'd go to that. I'm kind of into, like, big events and buildings and stuff, I take a lot of photos.
av_event.what: The bedroom door behind Isaac opens and a teenage girl (his sister) leans in, unplugs a phone charger from the socket by his shelf, and leaves again; Isaac's eyes flick sideways towards her for a second while he keeps talking.

text:
B: Alright? Can you hear me alright?
A: Yeah, hi, I'm Isaac. You're Darren, yeah?
B: That's me. Bridgwater, Somerset. You're the one with all them trainers in boxes, aren't you?
A: Ha, yeah, that's me. Guilty.
B: My son's the same. Proper fussy with his shoes. Won't let you near 'em.
A: Nah, to be fair, I'm the same. Some of them I actually sell on, though, so I have to keep them mint. I kind of run a little reselling business, like, limited releases. You buy them on drop day and sell them on for a bit more.
B: Do you? And people pay that?
A: Yeah, you'd be surprised. I just copped a pair last week I reckon I can get double for.
B: Double? Blimey. I've had my work boots about six years. Wouldn't get double for them.
A: Ha. What do you do, if you don't mind me asking?
B: Cleaning. Supermarket, early shifts. Up at half four, three mornings a week.
A: Half four? That's mad. I'm moaning about a nine o'clock lecture.
B: What you studying, then?
A: Economics, at City, in London. Second year.
B: Economics. So you'll be able to tell me why a pint's gone up to five quid down our local, then.
A: Erm, inflation, basically? Energy costs, the brewery passing it on. Sorry, that's a boring answer.
B: No, that's fair enough. Still daft, mind.
A: Nah, it is daft, you're right. Do you go out much, like, round Bridgwater?
B: Darts on a Thursday. Pub team. I'm no good, but it's a night out, d'you know what I mean. And carnival, November. That's the big one for us.
A: Carnival? Like Notting Hill?
B: Er, not really, no. It's the carts, big floats all lit up, thousands of bulbs, going through the town at night. Then the squibbing at the end, everybody holding these big fireworks up on poles, all down the high street. Sounds daft but it's proper. Been going every year since I was a nipper. Helped build a cart once with a mate's club. Took months.
A: Nah, that sounds actually sick. I'd go to that. I'm kind of into, like, big events and buildings and stuff, I take a lot of photos.
B: You should, it's free, mostly. You'd get some good pictures. Who d'you support, then? I saw the scarf.
A: Palace. Through my dad. We go to a couple of home games a season.
B: That's nice, that, going with your dad. I used to go City with mine. He's gone now, about eight years.
A: Oh, I'm sorry, man.
B: Ah, you're alright. Long time ago. What's the plan after, with the economics?
A: Erm, banking, hopefully, or consulting. I've got a spreadsheet of all the deadlines. My mum thinks it's a bit much.
B: Mums usually know. Nah, good on you, though. My lad never had a plan, he just—
